full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J:- The instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 17.11.2016 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Criminal Revision No. 332 of 2016 arising out of G.R No. 506 of 2016 (Sadar Dakkhin) and Comilla Sadar Dakkhin Police Station Case No. 60 dated 25.09.2016 disallowing the same and thereby affirming the order dated 03.10.2016 passed by the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, Cognizance Court No.09, Comilla rejecting the application for handing over the seized CARGO VAN being No Dhaka Metro-11-6812 bearing Engine No.VBE-15-0011Z, Cheeses No. MB I A3KWA8BRVE4174 into the custody of the petitioner that is to its real owner should not be quashed. 

 2. The prosecution case in short are that Md. Sahidul Islam, Sub Inspector of District Intelligence Branch, Comilla lodged an F.I.R on 25.09.2016 with the Officer-in-Charge of Comilla Sadar Dakkhin Policed Station, Comilla, alleging, inter alia, that while the informant was on duty on 25..09.2016 at about 00.05 A.M. received a information from secret source that one .Cargo van was going towards Chittagong from Comilla border by carrying drugs. After receiving the same on 25.09.2016 at 00.30 a.m. the informant along with forces went to Bhuiyan CNG Filling Station over the Dhaka-Chittagong High way under Comilla Sadar Dakkhin Police Station, Comilla Then after seeing the alleged cargo van on the place of occurrence at 00.40 A.M. the informant gave signal to stop the van. But the perpetrator after having came to know about the presence of the police they tried to flew away. But the police apprehended (1) Md. Zakir Hossain and (2) Riad Mia however one of them, namely, Rup Mia fled away. The Police force in the presence of the witnesses after searching the accused seized (1) 50 Kg Gaja (2) 2 Piecs Choter Bosta (3) 1 Cargo van, being Reg. No Dhaka-Metro-Ta-116812 from the possession of the accused persons. Upon query they admitted about the alleged occurrence and then police arrested the accused persons and prepared the seizure list in presence of the witnesses on 25.09.2016 at 00.55 A.M. Thereafter the informant went to Comilla Sadar Dakkhin Police Station, Comilla and lodged the F.I.R. 

 3. After receiving the F.1.R the Officer-in-Charge started Comilla Sadar Dakkhin Police Station Case No. 60 dated 25.09.2016 under Serial No.7 (Kha) of the table of Section 19(1) read with Sections 33(1)/25 of the Madok drobbo Niontron Ain, 1990 (Narcotics Control Act, 1990). The case was numbered as G.R. No. 506 of 2016 (Sadar Dakkhin). 

 4. The petitioner filed an application before the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, cognizance Court No. 9, Comilla for handing over the vehicle in his custody; however, unsuccessfully he preferred revision application before the Court of Sessions which was also rejected by the Court of Sessions. Hence, the petitioner preferred the instant Criminal Miscellaneous case for quashing the aforesaid Judgment and Order. 

 5. Mr. Shakhawat Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner purchase the vehicle in question obtaining loan from financial institute and if the same remain in custody under the Law enforcing Agency the petitioner will he failed to continuing to pay the installment against said vehicle and in that case the petitioner will suffer huge financial lose and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be quashed. He further adds that if the vehicle remain either in the open sky or in custody of law enforcing Agency the same will be destroyed, however, on the other hand if the same is handed over to the petitioner who is the owner by purchase the condition of the vehicle would be remained in good and the same condition would be maintained by him. He also added that there is no chance of early conclusion of the trial of the case, therefore, if the vehicle withheld up to the conclusion of the trial in that case the machineries of the vehicle would be destroyed and surely the condition of the vehicle would be out of order. Therefore, it needs to be hand over under the custody of the petitioner upon furnishing the proper surety. He also submits that if the vehicles handed over to the petitioner to ply the same on the road there is no chance to damage the same. He also pointed that if not handed over to the petitioner in that case the petitioner will suffer huge financial lose without any fault of him. 

 8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner; we also perused the documentary evidence produce by the learned Advocate by way of supplementary affidavit. On perusal the same it appears that the financial institute has already issued a certificate to the effect that all the dues have already been paid by the vendor of the petitioner and they have no objection regarding the transfer the same and register the same in the name of the Ifad Autos. The said Ifad Autos is the vendor of the petitioner i.e. the petitioner is purchaser of the vehicle which was used in carrying the some quantum of cannabis by the driver for which the vehicle was seized by the law enforcing Agencies. However, we are of the view that before final verdict if the vehicle in question is not released in favour of the petitioner and after conclusion of the trial if it is found that there is no connivance of the petitioner in committing the alleged offence and without any fault of him the vehicle in question go out of order in that case it would be the abuse of process of the Court. 

 More-so mere release of the vehicle it does not tantamount that the same has been released for ever or acquitted the vehicle from the charge of the offence. So, releasing the vehicle is as like as granting the bail of the accused. In the instant case if the accused can be released on bail why the vehicle would not be released on proper bond because it is mere change of custody. So, the view taken by the courts below cannot be sustained in law. We are therefore of the view that justice would be met if we direct the court below to release the aforesaid vehicle in favour of the petitioner by taking proper surety with condition to produce the vehicle as and when necessary by the court at the time of trial or at the time pronouncement of the judgment, otherwise the vehicle would be damaged due to non-maintenance. Consequently, it would be out of order in that case the petitioner will suffer financial loss without his fault. 

 11. The impugned order dated 17.11.2016 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, 3•d Court, Comilla in Criminal Revision No. 332 of 2016 and the order dated 03.10.2016 passed by the Senior Judicial Magistrate, Cognizance Court No. 9, Comilla in Comilla Sadar Dakkin Police Station case No. 60 dated 25.09.2016 are hereby quashed.
